# Sirach Chapter 37 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 37 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_037_page_001.jpg

---

37:1 Every friend says, "I too am a friend," but there is a friend who is only a friend in name.

37:2 Is it not a grief even unto death when a companion and friend turns to enmity?

37:3 O evil inclination! Why were you created to cover the dry land with deceit?

37:4 A false companion rejoices in the good fortune of a friend, but in time of trouble stands against him.

37:5 A true companion struggles with his friend against the belly, and in the face of the enemy takes up the shield.

37:6 Do not forget your companion in the battle, and do not neglect him when you divide the spoil.

37:7 Every counselor praises counsel, but some give counsel in their own interest.

37:8 Let your soul beware of a counselor, and find out first what his interest is — for he will take counsel for himself — lest the counsel fall upon you.

37:9 He might say to you, "Your way is good," and stand before you to watch what happens to you.

37:10 Do not take counsel with one who looks at you with suspicion; and hide your plan from those who envy you.

37:11 Do not take counsel with a woman about her rival, or with a coward about war, or with a merchant about business, or with a buyer about selling, or with an envious man about gratitude, or with the merciless about kindness, or with an idle person about any work, or with a hired laborer for a year about completing a task, or with a lazy servant about much work. Pay no attention to these in any matter of counsel.

37:12 Rather, consort with a godly man whom you know to be a keeper of the commandments, whose soul is in accord with your own soul, and who, if you stumble, will be sympathetic.

37:13 And set at nought the counsel of your own heart, for no one is more faithful to you than it is.

37:14 For a man's soul tends to keep him informed better than seven watchmen sitting on a height.

37:15 But above all of this, pray to the Most High that he may direct your way in truth.

37:16 The beginning of every work is a word, and before every action is deliberation.

37:17 The root of plans is the heart; it puts forth four branches:

37:18 good and evil, life and death, and the tongue which rules over them all has continual mastery.

37:19 A wise man will instruct many, but he himself may be of no use.

37:20 A man skillful in speech may be hated; he will be lacking in all food,

37:21 for grace was not given him from the Lord, since he is lacking in all wisdom.

37:22 There is one who is wise for himself, and the fruit of his understanding is trustworthy on his own lips.

37:23 A wise man instructs his people, and the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy.

37:24 A wise man will be filled with blessing, and all who see him will call him happy.

37:25 The days of a man's life are numbered, but the days of Israel are innumerable.

37:26 One who is wise among his people will inherit glory, and his name will live forever.

37:27 My son, test your soul during your lifetime, and see what is evil for it, and do not give it that.

37:28 For not everything is good for everyone, and not every soul finds pleasure in everything.

37:29 Do not be greedy for every luxury, and do not be poured out over many foods.

37:30 For overeating leads to sickness, and excess leads to colic.

37:31 Many have died from overeating, but the one who is careful adds to his life.
